newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips sink 3.27 percent at close.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips sink 3.27 percent at close.

text.p: Malaysian share prices crumpled on Monday under the pressure of Wall Street's 3.1 percent fall on Friday, and fears the ringgit would continue to slide against the dollar, said dealers and analysts.
The benchmark Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised issues closed down 29.73 points, 3.1 percent, at 880.45.
It earlier hit a new 30-month intraday low of 877.47, its weakest intraday level since January 27, 1995 when it dropped to 836.93.
"These two factors have definitely been the main reasons for the fall on the (Composite) index today," said a vice president of stock index futures trading at a local brokerage firm in Kuala Lumpur.
Small-capitalised shares also fared poorly, with the Second Board index dropping 14.23 points or 2.96 percent to 466.75. It hit a new 1997 low of 463.66 earlier in the day.

Volume topped 225 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 664 to 44. "I don't think there are any more major sellers. I expect the market to consolidate around the 880 level," said Ken Loo, head of research at Amsteel Securities.

On Friday the U.S. Dow Jones industrial average posted its second-largest point loss, falling 247.37 points, or 3.11 percent to 7,694.66, due to a weak U.S. dollar and over worries over U.S. corporate results.
The Malaysian currency weakened further on Monday. At 0800 GMT the ringgit stood at 2.7900 against the U.S. dollar. It had closed in Kuala Lumpur on Friday at 2.7780.
On Friday it broke above the 2.80 level to its lowest levels since it was first floated in 1973.
Rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Monday it had revised the outlook on Malaysia's long-term A-plus foreign currency and AA-plus local currency ratings to stable from positive.
S&P also said it had affirmed Malaysia's A1-plus short-term rating.
Stock debutante TT Resources closed at 5.00 ringgit after opening at 4.98 ringgit against a 2.50 ringgit offer price.
Maybank, Telekom and Tenaga lost between 35 cents and one ringgit. Conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd lost 20 cents to 7.70 ringgit.
Together the issues comprise 33 percent of the weightage of the Composite Index.
Telekom said on Sunday the continued depreciation of the ringgit would affect its bottom line as the company was exposed to foreign loans.
Maybank's fall was attributed to a reduction by foreign funds to Malaysia's finance sector.

At 0915 GMT on the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot August contract was down 23.5 points at 871.0 with 1,244 lots traded. September futures were down 22.0 points at 872.0 with seven lots traded.
